Bloomberg published a report yesterday pointing out that the future Apple Watch product line may see considerable changes.

The report specifically mentioned that Apple is exploring the possibility of launching one or more watches with a round rather than square design……

Most smartwatches are round.

Although square-faced watches have existed for over a century, most traditional watches are round, and the same goes for Android smartwatches. For example:

  • Amazfit Active Max
  • Samsung Galaxy Watch 9
  • Motorola Moto Watch
  • All Garmin models (Venu, Epix Pro, Forerunner, Fenix)
  • Google Pixel Watch

Apple's choice of a rectangular format is relatively unusual, so it would not be surprising if the company considered launching a round Apple Watch in the future.

The case for a round Apple Watch

Apple's original reason for choosing a rectangular design was to display more information. The screens we use every day — phones, tablets, laptops, monitors and so on — are all rectangular, and this is certainly no coincidence.

Ultimately, this trade-off is really a choice between aesthetics and practicality. There will always be people who prioritise practicality, so the rectangular Apple Watch will definitely not disappear. But there are also people who place great importance on appearance, and many have a strong preference for round watches (whether traditional or smart).

Furthermore, not everyone who wears an Apple Watch needs to view large amounts of information on the screen. Even if you rarely look at the watch screen, there are many benefits to wearing an Apple Watch. For example:

  • Health and fitness monitoring
  • Sleep tracking
  • Emergency features, such as fall detection
  • Contactless payment

Of the points above, health and fitness monitoring is the most attractive selling point for many people. If you mainly do not use your Apple Watch as a device for viewing content, then a round screen is perfectly viable for you.

But the case for an Apple Ring is even stronger

However, if you fall into this category of user — mainly using Apple Watch to monitor health and fitness, and not really using it to view information — I would argue that a smart ring is a smarter choice.

I myself switched from the Apple Watch to the Oura smart ring in 2024, and recently even upgraded to the fifth-generation model. I love how inconspicuous it is, that I can wear a traditional watch of my own choice, and that it only needs charging once a week.

Nearly two years ago, I already said that smart rings are a good alternative to the Apple Watch, and even believed that Apple should launch its own. To this day, I remain firmly convinced, and Gurman also says Eddy Cue is a big fan of smart rings, which shows the chances of a launch are quite high.

I do think Apple might launch a round Apple Watch, but I think what we're more likely to see is an Apple Ring. What do you think? Feel free to share your views in the comments.
